marble.name: Unit fractions
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Recognise, find, and write fractions of a discrete set of objects: unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators
marble.prompt: If there are 15 books on a shelf, can you work out how many two-thirds of them is — and check by grouping the books into three equal piles?

cluster.summary: Your child is discovering their first fractions — learning to recognise and name halves and quarters as equal parts of shapes, objects, and groups.

misconceptions: Takes the denominator as the answer: 1/4 of 12 is '4' because the fraction has a 4
For a non-unit fraction, finds 1/4 (=3) and stops, giving 3 for 3/4 instead of 9
Names a coloured set part-to-part (3 coloured, 9 not → 3/9) instead of part-to-whole (3/12)
Divides by the numerator instead of the denominator
representations: Counters shared into equal groups (12 → four groups of 3)
Bar model of the set partitioned into b parts with a shaded
Double number line (objects ↔ fraction of the set)
authoredAnswer: 1/4 of 12 = 3 (share into 4 equal groups of 3, take one group); 3/4 of 12 = 9 (take three of the four groups). The denominator 4 says how many equal groups to make; the numerator says how many groups to take — 4 is the number of groups, not the number of counters.
probe: Share 12 counters and establish that 1/4 of 12 is 3. Then, BEFORE sharing again, ask: 'What will 1/4 of these 8 counters be — the same 3, or different?' Have the child predict and give a reason. A child who believes a fraction names a fixed number of objects predicts 3; a child who understands the set is the whole pred

wrongAnswers.wrong: 4 counters (because the fraction has a 4 in it)
wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Selects 4 counters for 1/4 rather than sharing into 4 groups; tier-2 reason cites the digit
wrongAnswers.fix: Share the 12 into 4 equal groups on the tray; one group (3 counters) is 1/4. The 4 counts the GROUPS, not the objects.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Gives 3 for 3/4; does not take three of the four groups; cannot say the numerator means 'how many groups to take'
wrongAnswers.fix: Ask how many of the four groups 3/4 wants — three of them — and count 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: On the 'what fraction is coloured?' probe, compares coloured to uncoloured rather than to the whole set
wrongAnswers.fix: Count the coloured against the WHOLE set (all 12): 3 out of 12 = 3/12. The denominator is the whole, not the leftover.
